title: People v. Pepino
summary: The Supreme Court acquitted the accused for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act) due to the prosecution's failure to establish an unbroken chain of custody of the seized drugs. The integrity and evidentiary value of the corpus delicti were not preserved.
doctrine: In drug cases, the prosecution must establish an unbroken chain of custody of the seized drugs. Non-compliance with the chain of custody requirements under Section 21 of RA 9165 raises doubt on the integrity of the evidence and warrants acquittal. The corpus delicti must be preserved.
fullText:
BRION, J.:

The accused was charged with illegal sale and illegal possession of dangerous drugs under Sections 5 and 11 of RA 9165.

Section 21 of RA 9165 prescribes the procedure for the custody and disposition of confiscated drugs. The apprehending team must immediately conduct a physical inventory and photograph the seized items in the presence of the accused, a media representative, a DOJ representative, and an elected public official.

The failure to comply with these requirements, without justifiable grounds, casts doubt on the integrity and evidentiary value of the corpus delicti and constitutes a ground for acquittal.
